Adding the stationary equations gives Dρ′=vm, and subtracting gives Dm″−vρ′−2αm=0 and endpoint identity D²ρ″=v²ρ. The stated symmetric density solves these equations, normalizes to one, and gives nonnegative orientation densities: the possibly negative excess from the hyperbolic terms in ρ±Dρ′/v is bounded by q(Dκ/v−1)=1/(√(1+1/q)+1)<1. The mean reflecting regulator rate on a wall is D times its contact density, giving k_BT times that density as the force; independence of reflected coordinate processes justifies the exact tensorization. The displaced volume cancels the V in the pressure, giving the exact work differential. Since tanh(z)−z sech²(z) has positive derivative for z>0, F′>0 and the sum of the H terms is strictly Schur-convex at fixed log-volume. Anisotropy here is ordered by log-majorization, not by arbitrary scalar measures of shape. The even two-axis perturbation gives the stated quadratic coefficient; its derivative differs from q at positive infinity by an integrable exponential error. The Hessian is K−2nk_BT aF′(a); below threshold, evenness and coercivity give nonzero paired global minima. A trial t of order 1/K drives the minimum to minus infinity, so all positive minimizers diverge and stationarity yields Kt_K→nk_BTq.
